newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW -Italy March CPI seen at 2.2 pct yr/y.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -Italy March CPI seen at 2.2 pct yr/y.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the preliminary 0.1 percent rise in Italian March month-on-month CPI and the 2.2 year-on-year rate estimated after seven cities' inflation data released on Thursday.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast on average a month-on-month rate of 0.2 percent and a year-on-year rate of 2.3 percent.

Carmen Nuzzo, economist at Salomon Brothers in London, said: "These are very good figures and should point to a further slowing of inflation in March to 2.2 or 2.3 percent year-on-year. But a move (by the Bank of Italy) on interest rates is not imminent because of lira constraints."
Official CPI in February was 0.1 percent month on month and 2.4 percent year on year.

Ilaria Fornari at JP Morgan here said: "The numbers look slightly better than expectations. Even if we have a month on month rise in the other cities on Friday of 0.2 percent, slightly above average, then we're still on track for a 2.2 percent rate in March."

She saw inflation continuing to slow to 2.0 percent and below in coming months and given the weakness of the Italian economy and the high rate of real Italian interest rates, there was room for a possible interest rate cut in April.
"The one thing missing for the Bank of Italy to act is the mini budget," Fornari said.
The government is planning extra 1997 budget deficit cutting measures, which it will unveil once quarterly state accounts have been released. These are expected in coming days.

If a mini budget was unveiled by the end of next week and it reduced pressure on the lira, which has been weak against the mark recently, then the outlook for an interest rate cut was positive, Fornari said.
Rodolfo Dozio, economist at Banca Commerciale Italiana in Milan, said:
"We see the year-on-year rate falling below two percent in April. This is a much better than expected figure (for March) and there is more chance of 2.1 percent than 2.3 percent."
"If we take into account the positive statistical impact for April (the April 1996 figure was high) we see room for monetary easing if we just look at inflation," Dozio added.
Paolo Casadio, economist at Credito Italiano, said:
"It's a very positive figure above all if we consider that the data has not yet come out relative to the cities in the south which normally have higher inflation." Milan newsroom +392-66102321
